title: Wed Oct 28: Flexible circadian detection, biobank-scale synthetic genomes, and peering inside ESMFold's folding trunk
summary: 34 new papers. Deep dives: CircaFMM: A Flexible Statistical Framework for Circadian Rhythmicity Detection in Transcriptomics; Structure, Not Sequence: Tracking and Validating Folding Mechanisms in ESMFold's Trunk with Sparse Autoencoders; HELICS: Biobank-scale Conditional Synthetic Genome Generation via Latent Flow Matching; HGPRGDel: GPR-Aware Learning and Ranking for Growth-Coupled Gene Deletion Design; Enhancing Clinical Classifier Robustness with Deep Representation Learning Based OOD Detection on DNA Methylation Data
notes_html:
Deep dives

  1. CircaFMM: A Flexible Statistical Framework for Circadian Rhythmicity Detection in Transcriptomics — Joshua S. Abston et al.
    A flexible FMM-based alternative to Cosinor models for detecting circadian rhythmicity in irregular, asymmetric transcriptomic time series directly advances the statistical toolkit for sequencing-based gene expression analysis.
  2. Structure, Not Sequence: Tracking and Validating Folding Mechanisms in ESMFold's Trunk with Sparse Autoencoders — Bohan Liu et al.
    Using sparse autoencoders to reverse-engineer how ESMFold's trunk computes 3D structure from sequence offers a genuinely novel mechanistic window into structure prediction models that is highly relevant to systems/structural biology methods.
  3. HELICS: Biobank-scale Conditional Synthetic Genome Generation via Latent Flow Matching — Ahmad Abdel-Azim et al.
    A latent flow-matching generative model for biobank-scale SNP-level synthetic genomes, conditioned on ancestry and disease liability, is a significant methodological advance for genomics data augmentation and privacy-aware cohort simulation.
  4. HGPRGDel: GPR-Aware Learning and Ranking for Growth-Coupled Gene Deletion Design — Ziwei Yang et al.
    A GPR-aware learning-to-rank framework for growth-coupled gene deletion design bridges machine learning with constraint-based metabolic modeling, directly relevant to systems biology and strain engineering.
  5. Enhancing Clinical Classifier Robustness with Deep Representation Learning Based OOD Detection on DNA Methylation Data — Md Zahangir Alom et al.
    An out-of-distribution detection framework for DNA methylation-based tumor classifiers addresses a critical quality-control gap in clinical cancer genomics pipelines using deep representation learning.

Briefs

  1. Stationary Action Principles for Neuronal Growth — Nathan Brodeur et al.
    Variational/stochastic action principles for axonal growth guided by substrate mechanics connect biophysical modeling to measurable growth cone dynamics, a nice mechanistic systems biology angle outside sequencing.
  2. scPyviewer: a Python-native interactive viewer from AnnData single-cell data — Hao Xuan et al.
    A lightweight Python-native interactive viewer for AnnData objects fills a real gap for scanpy users who currently must convert to Seurat to share single-cell results.
  3. pyTransRate: 1 reference-free quality assessment of de novo transcriptome assemblies with current aligners and quantifiers — Matthew MacManes
    A modernized, dependency-free reimplementation of TransRate gives de novo transcriptome assemblers a reference-free QC tool that actually still runs on current systems.
  4. ACOR: incremental evidence accumulation towards real-time DNA storage reconstruction — Linxuan Han et al.
    A streaming consensus-reconstruction algorithm for DNA storage achieves near real-time decoding of noisy synthetic DNA reads, relevant to the computational side of DNA-based data storage.
  5. The uneven rise of AI-generated web content — Adam Visokay et al.
    A large-scale Bayesian measurement-error-corrected analysis finds AI-generated text is growing fastest on the least-central, least-trafficked parts of the web, a surprising structural finding about the internet's information ecosystem.
  6. Balanced State Subspaces for Mamba-2 State Compression — Shang Tingyu et al.
    A balanced-truncation approach to compressing Mamba-2's recurrent state by finding the true write-read subspace nearly halves memory with much smaller perplexity loss than existing quantization/pruning methods.
  7. Close Races and Similarity Bias: A Bayesian Analysis of the Ranked Ballots for the Ballon d'Or — Guanyu Hu et al.
    A Bayesian mixture-of-experts model for partial rankings quantifies how voter 'style' and regional affinity bias Ballon d'Or outcomes, a clever application of rank data modeling to a contested real-world judgment problem.
  8. Relaxed MEMs: Enhancing Borrowing in Multisource Exchangeability Models for Small Sample Applications — Shannon D. Thomas et al.
    Relaxed Multisource Exchangeability Models loosen overly conservative borrowing limits in small-sample rare-disease trials, improving efficiency with minimal bias cost.
  9. Is Your LLM Relay Serving What It Claims? A low-cost and high-power test for LLM Relay Auditing — Fangran Miao et al.
    A distributional-fingerprint statistical test lets users detect whether an LLM relay API is silently serving a substituted model, with calibrated p-values and substitution-ratio estimation.
  10. Causal DAG-Guided Reinforcement Learning for Long-Term Physical Activity Maintenance: Using Prior Data to Inform Future Deployment — Xueqing Liu et al.
    This causal-DAG-guided reinforcement learning design for a digital health physical-activity trial shows how domain knowledge and simulators can make long-horizon personalized interventions deployable despite sparse, delayed rewards.

Quick mentions

  1. Dynamic Properties of Numerical Solution for Stochastic Epidemic Models with a Fully Implicit Form — Zeyao Jin et al.
    A fully implicit numerical scheme for stochastic epidemic models proves convergence and shows environmental noise can drive disease extinction.
  2. Bayesian Ordinal Analysis of Cereal Growth Stage Data from Oat Trials in Western Australia — Zhanglong Cao et al.
    A Bayesian hierarchical ordinal model with spatial structure analyzes cereal growth-stage scores from oat trials, showing deeper sowing accelerates early development.
  3. Finite-population inference for cross-fitted estimators of treatment contrasts in stratified multistage surveys — M. Ehsan Karim
    New finite-population theory for cluster-respecting cross-fitted double machine learning estimators gives more honest variance estimates for treatment effects in stratified health surveys.
  4. Causal sensitivity analyses for indirect and spillover mediation effects in cluster-randomized trials: Application to a pragmatic trial on chronic pain management — Yuki Ohnishi et al.
    A two-part sensitivity analysis for cross-world mediation assumptions in a cluster-randomized chronic pain trial shows mechanistic pathway claims are highly assumption-dependent.
  5. Penalized Cause-Specific Hazard Regression under Competing Risks: An Elastic Net Approach Using SANAD Trial Data — Avinash Kumar
    An elastic-net-regularized generalized exponential regression for competing risks improves estimate stability over standard cause-specific hazard models in a stroke trial dataset.
  6. Estimating the Effect of a Low Nicotine Standard on Smoking Behavior in the U.S. Population — Milena I. Silva (Division of Biostatistics and Health Data Science et al.
    A novel transportability estimator accounting for treatment non-adherence estimates how a near-total nicotine reduction standard would affect smoking behavior in the broader U.S. population.
  7. Bayesian Recovery Trajectories Following Forced Sexual Experience: Healthcare Access and Social Support Among Women — Hammed A. Olayinka et al.
    A Bayesian mixture model identifies three distinct long-term health trajectories after forced sexual violence, with healthcare access and social support as modifiable protective factors.
  8. Practical Guidelines for Goodness-of-Fit Testing for Right-Censored Data — Arnau G\'omez-Catal\`a et al.
    A simulation study gives practical guidance on when Kolmogorov-Smirnov, Anderson-Darling, or Cramér-von Mises goodness-of-fit tests perform best for right-censored survival data.
  9. Personal preference or system role? Battery swapping among UK electric vehicle users — Janak Parmar et al.
    A choice-latent-variable model finds UK EV users evaluate battery swapping differently as a personal purchase decision versus a system-level transport technology.
  10. Reconstructing the Human Development Index at the Individual Level from Survey Microdata: Development and Validation of a Methodology — Tcharlies Bachmann Schmitz (PX Center et al.
    A method to reconstruct individual-level HDI scores from survey microdata achieves high agreement with official national HDI values, enabling disaggregated development analysis.

title: Mon Oct 26: Clonal pseudoreplication in Perturb-seq benchmarks, enhancer target selection by partition, and the evolutionary origin of loop extrusion
summary: 170 new papers. Deep dives: Shared clones make random cell halves look reproducible in pooled screens; Regulation by partition predicts enhancer target selection in mammalian genomes; Inference and validation of causal genetic interactions in aging human fibroblasts; Reference-free isoform discovery links unannotated RNA processing to disease risk; Evolution of CTCF underlies the establishment of loop extrusion as a predominant chromatin folding mechanism in vertebrates
notes_html:
Deep dives

  1. Shared clones make random cell halves look reproducible in pooled screens — Xuanrui Huang
    Shows that standard random-half reproducibility metrics for pooled Perturb-seq screens are massively inflated by shared clonal lineages, a finding with direct implications for how every single-cell perturbation-prediction benchmark should be designed and interpreted.
  2. Regulation by partition predicts enhancer target selection in mammalian genomes — Valgardson, J. et al.
    A large-scale synthetic enhancer-insertion screen (SPIE-seq) reveals that enhancer target choice is governed by distance-weighted competition among promoters rather than enhancer or promoter identity alone, yielding a transferable 'Regulation-by-Partition' model of gene regulation.
  3. Inference and validation of causal genetic interactions in aging human fibroblasts — Krieger, M. S. et al.
    Demonstrates that convergent cross-mapping can recover causal gene-gene interaction networks from cross-sectional (not longitudinal) human transcriptomic data, and experimentally validates predicted anti-aging perturbations in fibroblasts—a striking proof that causal dynamics can be extracted from population snapshots.
  4. Reference-free isoform discovery links unannotated RNA processing to disease risk — Buen Abad Najar, C. F. et al.
    Introduces Torino, an annotation-free NMF-based framework for discovering RNA processing events directly from coverage data, uncovering thousands of disease-linked splicing/intron-retention QTLs missed by transcript-database-dependent methods, including in Alzheimer's brain.
  5. Evolution of CTCF underlies the establishment of loop extrusion as a predominant chromatin folding mechanism in vertebrates — Astica, L. et al.
    Cross-species functional replacement of CTCF orthologs in mouse ESCs and Drosophila embryos pinpoints when and how CTCF acquired its loop-extrusion-mediated TAD-forming function during bilaterian evolution, directly bearing on the molecular basis of chromatin architecture.

Briefs

  1. SPATNIC enables H&E-grounded cancer-cell identification across spatial and single-cell transcriptomic modalities in colorectal cancer — Sakai, S. A. et al.
    SPATNIC is a pathologist-annotation-trained classifier that generalizes zero-shot across six spatial and single-cell platforms to call cancer vs. normal cells, a practically useful building block for spatial transcriptomics tumor analyses.
  2. ResponseVerdict overturns computationally validated immunotherapy signatures, recovers their missed responders and outperforms every published response predictor — Jiang, H. et al.
    A sharp critique showing that the vast majority of published immune-checkpoint response gene signatures perform no better than random gene sets when properly validated, with a new scoring method that substantially improves patient stratification.
  3. Genome-wide LD scores enable robust heritability and genetic correlation estimation from summary statistics across genetic ancestries — Jeong, M. et al.
    SUMMIT uses efficiently computed genome-wide LD scores to improve heritability and genetic correlation estimation in admixed and non-European cohorts, addressing a major gap in complex trait genetics across ancestries.
  4. Chromosomal instability drives continual flux in cancer genomes — Guscott, M. A. et al.
    Single-cell genome sequencing across multiple cancer types shows chromosomal instability generates 1-5 new copy-number alterations per cell cycle, revealing cancer genomes as being in continual structural flux rather than static end-states.
  5. Averaging in gene perturbation benchmarks hides perturbation-strength variation: Consequences for model evaluation — Sharma, Y. S. et al.
    Shows that averaging cells per perturbation in CRISPRi screens discards perturbation-strength information that current state-of-the-art perturbation-prediction models (STATE, Cell2Sentence) fail to recover, a cautionary note for the whole perturbation-modeling field.
  6. Haplotype-based fine-mapping of variant associations for complex traits — Massarat, A. R. et al.
    happler extends statistical fine-mapping to haplotypes rather than individual variants, recovering causal signals—including for ungenotyped structural variants—that standard per-SNP fine-mapping misses.
  7. Denoising single-cell ATAC-seq data with Shannon entropy — Yang, S. et al.
    A simple Shannon-entropy-based nucleus-filtering approach improves signal-to-noise and rare population detection in scATAC-seq, addressing a persistent quality-control bottleneck in chromatin accessibility profiling.
  8. Decoding Cell-level Circadian Phase and Rhythm-state Remodeling in Single-cell Transcriptomes With scRhythmBayes — Zhang, Q. et al.
    scRhythmBayes infers cell-level circadian phase and rhythm-state remodeling from heterogeneous single-cell transcriptomes, revealing a hidden temporal dimension of liver zonation and cell identity.
  9. Computational modeling of breast cancer metastases predicts response to dual checkpoint inhibition and reveals spatially-informed treatments — King, T. et al.
    An agent-based model of the breast-to-lung metastatic tumor microenvironment predicts which metastases respond to dual checkpoint blockade and identifies Treg colocalization with CD8 T cells as a resistance mechanism and therapeutic target.

Quick mentions

  1. RNA m6A mediates de novo DNA methylation and heritable epigenetic silencing in human cells — Divekar, N. S. et al.
    Finds that RNA m6A writer recruitment to chromatin is required for de novo DNA methylation and heritable epigenetic silencing in human cells, linking the epitranscriptome directly to genome defense against transposable elements.
  2. Systematic mapping of the prokaryotic noncoding sequence space with a genomic language model — Sun, G. et al.
    A genomic language model organizes 376 million prokaryotic intergenic regions into millions of clusters, uncovering thousands of candidate novel structured RNA families including new bridge-RNA variants.
  3. Panagram reveals pangenome architectures underlying trait variation in plants and animals — Jenike, K. M. et al.
    Panagram's alignment-free pan-k-mer framework links pangenome structural variation to traits from Arabidopsis flowering time to dog facial morphology across hundreds of genomes.
  4. Dissecting cellular and molecular networks of aging and senescence in the human hippocampus — De Los Santos, M. B. et al.
    A multimodal spatial and single-nucleus atlas of the aging human hippocampus identifies sex-dependent senescence programs and divergence between classic senescence markers p16 and p21.
  5. Recurrent leukaemia stem cell states define the antigenic landscape of paediatric Acute Myeloid Leukaemia — Kanannejad, S. et al.
    Single-cell and CITE-seq profiling of pediatric AML reveals three coexisting leukemia stem cell states and proposes a CLEC12A/CD84 dual-targeting strategy for CAR T-cell design.
  6. Large-scale integrated single-cell analysis reveals molecular subtypes and microenvironmental remodeling in cutaneous T cell lymphoma — Reis, R. J. et al.
    The largest integrated single-cell atlas of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma to date defines molecular subtypes with prognostic value using rigorous pseudobulk mixed-effects modeling to avoid pseudoreplication.
  7. Multi-scale microenvironment covariance for unsupervised spatial domain identification — Du, B. et al.
    CoSMIM represents tissue niches via multi-scale gene-gene covariance rather than mean expression, improving unsupervised spatial domain identification across diverse spatial transcriptomics platforms.
  8. Maternal E-cigarette Exposure Augments Murine Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm — Spin, J. M. et al.
    A statistical survey of thousands of vertebrate mitochondrial genomes finds convergent gene-order rearrangements at the WANCY region are more frequent than previously appreciated, informing mitochondrial genome evolution models.
  9. CTCF gradually acquires novel function modalities during bilaterian evolution — Nurislamov, A. et al.
    A companion evolutionary study shows CTCF progressively gained proximity to transcription start sites and nucleosome-phasing ability across bilaterian lineages, complementing functional-replacement evidence for CTCF's gradual acquisition of architectural roles.
  10. The effects of DNA repair factor-Cas9 fusions on homing drive performance — Wu, Y. et al.
    Systematic testing of Cas9-DNA repair protein fusions in Drosophila gene drives identifies Cas9-POLD3 and Cas9-Geminin as context-specific tools to boost homing drive conversion and limit resistance alleles.

title: Thu Oct 22: Cell-state-aware sequence models, in silico lineage tracing, and cleaning up off-target noise in Perturb-seq
summary: 130 new papers. Deep dives: Predicting cell-state-specific gene regulation from DNA across species; Virtual lineages: in silico lineage tracing from single-cell and spatial transcriptomes; PETRO enables robust estimation of on-target perturbation effects in Perturb-seq; A genomic foundation model for interpreting human genetic diversity; When do hybrid models help? Combining mechanistic modelling and machine learning to predict gene regulatory network dynamics
notes_html:
Deep dives

  1. Predicting cell-state-specific gene regulation from DNA across species — Liu, H. et al.
    Bolero conditions a sequence-to-function model on atlas-scale cell-state embeddings to predict cell-state-specific chromatin accessibility and expression from DNA, unifying sequence models and single-cell foundation models for regulatory genomics across species.
  2. Virtual lineages: in silico lineage tracing from single-cell and spatial transcriptomes — Lin, Y. et al.
    isCORAL infers clonal lineage relationships and cell-fate dynamics directly from single-cell/spatial transcriptomes using heritable 'memory genes,' offering a scalable alternative to experimental lineage tracing for development and cancer studies.
  3. PETRO enables robust estimation of on-target perturbation effects in Perturb-seq — Sun, Z. et al.
    PETRO is a robust statistical framework for Perturb-seq that recovers on-target perturbation effects while tolerating off-target guide behavior, addressing a core methodological pitfall in CRISPR screen analysis.
  4. A genomic foundation model for interpreting human genetic diversity — Xu, Q. et al.
    hEVO, a genomic foundation model trained on nearly 5 billion haplotypes, outperforms Evo2/NT/GPN on variant interpretation, functional annotation, and evolutionary inference with far fewer parameters, a significant advance in regulatory/variant genomics.
  5. When do hybrid models help? Combining mechanistic modelling and machine learning to predict gene regulatory network dynamics — Noordijk, B. et al.
    A systematic study of when hybrid mechanistic+ML models improve gene regulatory network dynamics prediction over either approach alone, directly addressing a central open question in GRN inference methodology.

Briefs

  1. An autoencoder outperforms two transformers on prediction of gene expression from chromatin accessibility — Jesse G. Meyer
    A rigorous benchmark finds a simple dual-VAE architecture (scButterfly-B) beats transformer-based models including a Perceiver and Cisformer variant at predicting gene expression from chromatin accessibility, a useful reality check against hype in multi-omics modeling.
  2. SP1 tethers NR2F2 to drive atrial cardiomyocyte identity — Gergen, P. N. et al.
    Combining GRN inference from human fetal scRNA/ATAC-seq with AlphaFold and experimental validation reveals SP1 tethers NR2F2 to drive atrial cardiomyocyte identity, a nice case study in regulatory network dissection.
  3. Carbon-A: Unified Genome Annotation across Eukaryotic Diversity — Channing, G. et al.
    Carbon-A, a 1.2B-parameter model, delivers state-of-the-art eukaryotic gene annotation across the tree of life and is used to build a reference-free annotation database nine times larger than RefSeq.
  4. Phenotype-cloud reorganization shapes cancer progression and therapeutic adaptation — Zhang, Y. et al.
    Integrating spatial, single-cell, and proteomic data, this study maps reproducible 'phenotype-cloud' transitions during breast cancer progression and therapeutic adaptation, linking tumor heterogeneity to a conserved fitness architecture.
  5. A clinically annotated proteomic and histological resource of 1,000 colorectal cancers — Qoku, A. et al.
    The largest proteomically profiled CRC cohort (1,000 cases) resolves chromosomally unstable tumors into functional subgroups with distinct outcomes, a major resource for cancer heterogeneity research.
  6. Genome-scale base editing reveals the functional effects of variants in yeast — Boocock, J. et al.
    Genome-scale CRISPR base editing measures growth effects of over 300,000 coding and noncoding variants in yeast, providing a systematic nucleotide-resolution map of genotype-to-phenotype relationships.
  7. Extrachromosomal circular DNA formation follows a 10.5-bp periodicity reflecting the minor groove orientation around nucleosomes — Zabala, A. et al.
    A clever Fourier analysis of eccDNA length distributions reveals that circular DNA breakpoints follow the 10.5-bp helical periodicity of nucleosome-bound DNA, giving a structural mechanism for extrachromosomal DNA biogenesis relevant to cancer genomics.
  8. A pan-cancer catalog of mutagenesis at transcription factor binding sites — Sahay, H. et al.
    A pan-cancer catalog of mutation enrichment at transcription factor binding sites across 4,000+ tumors links TF binding, DNA damage and repair to noncoding mutagenesis, informing interpretation of regulatory mutations in cancer.
  9. XplainTDA: Explaining the topological structure of single-cell multi-omics data through perturbation — Giray, I. et al.
    XplainTDA extends persistent homology on single-cell multi-omics point clouds with a perturbation-based explainability layer, moving topological data analysis from description to molecular interpretation.
  10. Simulation-free approximate Bayesian computation for stochastic reaction networks — Li, Z. et al.
    A simulation-free approximate Bayesian computation framework exploits the Chemical Master Equation directly, matching standard ABC accuracy at much lower cost for inferring stochastic reaction networks from single-cell data.

Quick mentions

  1. MINT Block: multivariate integration across independent studies to identify multi-omics signatures — Hirst, D. P. et al.
    MINT Block jointly integrates multi-omics data across independent studies while correcting for study-specific variation without distorting biological signal.
  2. Optimal transport reveals unresolved cells in single cell multi-omics — Piran, M. et al.
    An optimal-transport framework makes cross-modality cell matching explicit in single-cell multi-omics integration, flagging ambiguous/unresolved cells that existing tools silently mishandle.
  3. Combining RNA-seq and proteomics boosts sensitivity to detect differentially expressed genes by rpMeta — Zhang, X. et al.
    rpMeta improves sensitivity for differential expression detection by meta-analyzing paired RNA-seq and proteomics data rather than analyzing each separately.
  4. X-SPEAR: An Extensible Framework for Spatial Panel Evaluation and Refinement — Patel, R. et al.
    X-SPEAR couples interpretable marker selection with detection-aware training to design better targeted spatial transcriptomics gene panels for platforms like Xenium.
  5. GOLDEN: Gene expression and allele-informed decomposition for genetic heterogeneity in spatial transcriptomic data — Paik, H.
    GOLDEN uses allele-aware deep learning to deconvolve genetic heterogeneity (e.g., placental/allograft mosaicism) in spatial transcriptomics spots.
  6. Developmental origins of thymic B-cell lymphomas — Rai, S. et al.
    Single-cell multiomics and spatial profiling trace a thymus-specific B-cell differentiation program that is redeployed in thymic B-cell lymphomagenesis, linking development and cancer.
  7. Ascorbate is a physiological tumor suppressor metabolite in leukemia — Wijshake, T. et al.
    A surprising finding that ascorbate acts as a physiological tumor suppressor metabolite in leukemia, with depletion in hematopoietic cells sufficient to drive leukemogenesis via TET2/3.
  8. Inflammation is an essential trigger for POLE-driven ultramutated colorectal cancer — Mustofa, M. K. et al.
    A mouse model shows inflammation is required to unleash POLE-driven hypermutated colorectal cancer, revealing an unexpected gatekeeper role for genomic proofreading mutations.
  9. APLNR regulates directed migration to spatially pattern mesoderm in human gastruloids — Johnson, A. B. et al.
    APLNR-mediated chemotaxis is shown to spatially pattern mesoderm progenitor positioning in human gastruloids, linking directed cell migration to tissue patterning during gastrulation.

title: Tue Oct 20: Fixing double-dipping in topic models and perturbation benchmarks, a compact enhancer logic for fibrosis, and sequence-to-function fine-mapping of GWAS variants
summary: 233 new papers. Deep dives: Reducing double-dipping in single-cell topic models with three-way count splitting; A Pitfall in the Evaluation of Gene Perturbation Models; A Compact Regulatory Logic Governs Fibroblast Cell State Plasticity in Fibrosis; GEMS (GWAS Effect Mechanisms via Sequence-to-Function): Unveiling cell type-specific mechanisms for GWAS variants; MOFI reveals dynamic multi-omics coordination during cell fate progression
notes_html:
Deep dives

  1. Reducing double-dipping in single-cell topic models with three-way count splitting — Zheng Qu
    Shows that naive and even two-way count-split inference in single-cell topic models massively inflates false discoveries (36-59% vs nominal 5%), and introduces a three-way splitting fix validated on lupus and COVID cohorts—directly relevant to anyone fitting gene-program models to scRNA-seq.
  2. A Pitfall in the Evaluation of Gene Perturbation Models — George Panagopoulos et al.
    A rigorous audit of gene-perturbation model benchmarks reveals that a common prediction-replication artifact inflates precision scores and flips 'winning' methods 87% of the time depending on DE-gene cutoff, with real implications for how the field should evaluate Perturb-seq models.
  3. A Compact Regulatory Logic Governs Fibroblast Cell State Plasticity in Fibrosis — Zhu, A. M. et al.
    A massive CROP-seq enhancer-repression screen (550,000 fibroblasts, 280 enhancers) distills fibroblast activation into a compact regulatory logic centered on MEOX1, and shows just six enhancers can collapse the profibrotic network—an elegant GRN-to-phenotype study with direct disease relevance.
  4. GEMS (GWAS Effect Mechanisms via Sequence-to-Function): Unveiling cell type-specific mechanisms for GWAS variants — Xie, X. et al.
    GEMS combines sequence-to-function models (Borzoi) with SHAP attribution to assign GWAS variants to the cell types and regulatory mechanisms driving them, cleanly separating immune vs CNS modules in multiple sclerosis—exactly the kind of variant-to-regulation inference the profile prioritizes.
  5. MOFI reveals dynamic multi-omics coordination during cell fate progression — Shen, J. et al.
    MOFI reconstructs continuous multi-omic cell-fate trajectories from discrete paired snapshots by jointly modeling omics-specific dynamics, cross-omics correspondence and population growth, demonstrated across kidney organoid, hematopoietic and brain organoid systems—a strong synthesis of multi-omics integration and developmental trajectory inference.

Briefs

  1. Order Matters: Ambient RNA correction confounds doublet detection in single-cell RNA sequencing — Meier, M. et al.
    A simple but important methodological finding: running ambient-RNA correction before doublet detection (the common pipeline order) masks doublets, and the authors show doublet detection should come first except when using CellBender.
  2. Navigating the rapidly evolving landscape of sequencing-based spatial transcriptomics technologies: a comprehensive multi-platform benchmark — Mortier, J. et al.
    A systematic multi-platform benchmark of sequencing-based spatial transcriptomics technologies offers practical, much-needed guidance on capture efficiency and spatial accuracy trade-offs across the rapidly proliferating set of commercial platforms.
  3. On technical biases in imaging spatial transcriptomics — Chen, C. et al.
    Categorizes and models the experimental and computational technical biases compounding in imaging-based spatial transcriptomics, proposing a unified count-modeling framework to formalize these artifacts.
  4. Survival-associated cellular communication networks in human solid cancers — Lee, D. et al.
    SKyNet integrates a pan-cancer single-cell atlas with TCGA survival data to prioritize ligand-receptor interactions with clinical significance, validating endothelial-pericyte and lymphatic signaling axes tied to patient outcomes.
  5. Determining cellular phylogeny and migration at high resolution in spatial genomics — Zhang, D. et al.
    StarTrak performs somatic-variant-based lineage reconstruction directly in spatial genomics data, revealing tumor cell migration into adjacent tissue and UV-mutant epidermal cell migration into deeper skin layers.
  6. scRBP infers cell-specific RNA-binding protein regulons from single-cell transcriptomes at gene and isoform resolution — Ma, Y. et al.
    scRBP extends single-cell regulatory network inference beyond transcription factors to RNA-binding proteins, recovering eCLIP-validated targets and CRISPRi-responsive programs across 6.2 million cells—filling a real gap in post-transcriptional regulatory inference.
  7. A relational architecture of the human genome — Kurth, I. et al.
    A striking (and likely to be debated) claim: exhaustive in-silico mutagenesis with a genomic language model reveals a directed network of position-to-position dependencies across the whole human genome, dubbed 'relons', suggesting a higher-order relational layer of genome organization.
  8. Decoding the naked mole-rat genome, telomere to telomere — Sokolowski, D. J. et al.
    A telomere-to-telomere, haplotype-resolved naked mole-rat genome resolves satellite-free centromeres and the Y chromosome, and identifies gene losses/duplications tied to its famous cancer resistance and longevity—a landmark resource outside the core focus but broadly important.
  9. Simulation-free approximate Bayesian computation for stochastic reaction networks — Zekai Li et al.
    SFABC reformulates approximate Bayesian computation for stochastic reaction networks as a convex optimization over the Chemical Master Equation, avoiding costly Gillespie simulation while provably converging to the true posterior—applied to single-cell transcriptional bursting data.
  10. The pan-cancer whole-genome landscape of Adolescent and Young Adult solid cancers — van Putten, J. et al.
    A large pan-cancer whole-genome comparison of adolescent/young-adult versus older-adult tumors shows that most apparent age-related genomic differences actually reflect age-skewed cancer subtypes rather than AYA-specific mutagenesis, with notable germline enrichment.

Quick mentions

  1. STING deficiency extends median lifespan and mitigates age-related liver pathology in mice — Martinez, J. C. C. et al.
    Genetic deletion of STING extends median mouse lifespan and blunts age-related liver pathology, a striking longevity result implicating chronic cGAS-STING inflammation in aging.
  2. Telomere dynamics parameters inferred from mathematical modeling of telomere length distribution — Gavilanes Guerrero, V. et al.
    A mathematical (ergodic Markov chain) model of telomere length distributions from long-read sequencing infers telomerase kinetic parameters across 66 yeast strains, including chromosome-end-specific regulation.
  3. Dynamic TET1 repression coordinates activation of macroH2A.2-poised bivalent genes during neuroectoderm differentiation — Terry, B. et al.
    TET1 is shown to act non-catalytically with the histone variant macroH2A.2 to poise bivalent chromatin, then selectively disengage to permit neuroectoderm gene activation during differentiation.
  4. Genetic Perturbation Prediction Models Fail Out-of-Distribution: A Rigorous Benchmark and Systematic Evaluation — Tiwari, K. et al.
    A rigorous out-of-distribution benchmark shows perturbation-prediction models, including single-cell foundation models, degrade substantially and gain no reliable edge over simple baselines once tested outside their training distribution.
  5. Auditing Confidence-Calibrated Benchmarking of Single-Cell Perturbation Models — Gallone, M. et al.
    An audit of single-cell perturbation benchmarking harnesses exposes six concrete failure modes—including an 'echo ceiling' from scoring models against their own input—that make most headline uncertainty/calibration results misleading.
  6. Variable sparsity non-negative matrix and tensor factorization algorithms and their applications in cancer genomics — Pham, T. et al.
    Introduces variable-sparsity NMF/NTF algorithms giving fine-grained, per-component control over sparsity for cancer genomics data, bridging generative parts-based and partitional clustering representations.
  7. Biopsy-aware phylogenetic reconstruction from longitudinal single-cell copy number profiles — Paszek, J. et al.
    A biopsy-aware phylogenetic framework for longitudinal single-cell copy-number data outperforms pooled methods by respecting sample collection order, improving reconstruction of cancer clonal ancestry.
  8. Dynamic flux balance analysis of cancer metabolism using expression-based human cell line models — Kelley, L. P. et al.
    Dynamic flux balance analysis across multiple expression-calibrated cancer cell-line metabolic models reveals media- and lineage-dependent flux dynamics and sets up virtual tumor-stroma competition simulations.
  9. How Robust Are Prognostic Radiomic Features? Comparing Selection Techniques on Pooled Glioblastoma Cohorts — Yannick Sodonougbo et al.
    Shows that choice of feature-selection method (log-rank vs Cox vs SHAP/XGBoost) substantially changes which radiomic features appear prognostic in pooled glioblastoma cohorts, cautioning against over-interpreting single-pipeline radiomics signatures.

title: Fri Oct 16: Spatial noise versus signal, genotype bias in methylomes, and what trophectoderm genes are doing in your tumour
summary: 61 new papers. Deep dives: Biological and technical spatial variation in spatial transcriptomics; Mitigating genotype-driven bias improves atlas-scale single-cell DNA methylome profiling; Panoramic modelling of single-cell transcriptomes at scale with CellNet; Deciphering Spatial Cellular Organization through RNA-Anchored Multi-Omics Deconvolution; Pervasive expression of early embryonic programs in cancer has stage-dependent survival impact
notes_html:
Deep dives

  1. Biological and technical spatial variation in spatial transcriptomics — Jackson, K. C. et al.
    Introduces a bursty-transcription model (stipple) to disentangle genuine spatially variable gene expression from spatially variable capture/technical noise in spatial transcriptomics, directly addressing a core methodological gap in the field.
  2. Mitigating genotype-driven bias improves atlas-scale single-cell DNA methylome profiling — Song, X. et al.
    Shows that unmasked genetic variants confound bisulfite-based single-cell methylation calls and provides a practical variant-masking fix that improves batch mixing in atlas-scale scMethylome studies.
  3. Panoramic modelling of single-cell transcriptomes at scale with CellNet — Xiaoqing Lian et al.
    CellNet is a 231-million-profile, 40-species single-cell foundation model that unifies RNA expression and gene identity in a shared representation, improving rare cell-state detection and cross-species/cross-modality prediction.
  4. Deciphering Spatial Cellular Organization through RNA-Anchored Multi-Omics Deconvolution — Bai, Y. et al.
    SMODER offers an RNA-anchored deconvolution framework for spatial multi-omics (protein, ATAC, histone marks) that preserves cell-type identifiability while denoising co-profiled modalities, a key multi-omics integration advance.
  5. Pervasive expression of early embryonic programs in cancer has stage-dependent survival impact — Wang, T. et al.
    Using machine-learning classifiers of preimplantation transcriptional programs across large cancer cohorts, this study finds that resemblance to early embryonic stages has stage-dependent and sometimes protective prognostic effects, linking developmental biology to cancer systems biology and actionable dependencies (MYBL2/FOXM1).

Briefs

  1. 2,234 attempts to harmonize a multi-platform B-cell lymphoma bulk transcriptomic dataset: ComBat is superior by cross-batch prediction quality — Nikitin, D. et al.
    A massive benchmark (2,234 harmonization pipelines) on B-cell lymphoma transcriptomes shows that the 'best' batch-correction method depends entirely on which evaluation metric class you choose, with real implications for anyone doing cross-platform RNA-seq integration.
  2. Systematic evaluation of transcript normalization methods and quantification pipelines across long-read sequencing platforms — Paniagua, A. et al.
    Systematic benchmark of transcript quantification normalization across PacBio and Nanopore long-read platforms reveals platform-specific length biases that standard short-read normalization methods fail to correct.
  3. Alpha Spatial: Language-guided prediction of single-cell spatial gene expression from histology — YANG, X. et al.
    Alpha Spatial predicts single-cell spatial gene expression from histology using language-conditioned multi-tissue learning, recovering clinically relevant stromal and HER2-associated spatial programs in breast cancer.
  4. Global signatures of Ribonucleotide Excision Repair deficiency and its therapeutic vulnerabilities — Toong, P. J. et al.
    Identifies a mutational-signature-based classifier (RERDetect) for ribonucleotide excision repair deficiency across 11,000+ tumors, uncovering a previously hidden DNA-repair-deficient cancer subtype with druggable vulnerabilities.
  5. Dual-graph deconvolution of enzyme fitness: an interpretable framework to identify and explain catalytic modulators — Garcia Busto, S. et al.
    A hybrid stability-predictor/coevolution-graphical-model framework isolates stability-independent activity effects of mutations, offering an interpretable alternative to black-box protein language model deconvolution for enzyme engineering.
  6. Programmable design of functional RNAs through multimodal generative learning — Ma, J. et al.
    RNAverse is a multimodal generative model spanning RNA sequence, structure probing and function that designs novel functional RNAs (aptamers, UTRs, aptazymes) validated experimentally, including boosting vaccine antibody responses in mice.
  7. A microbiota-driven neuroepithelial feed-forward circuit drives gastroesophageal junction tumorigenesis — Zeng, Y. et al.
    Describes a microbiota-neuron-epithelium feed-forward circuit at the gastroesophageal junction that drives tumorigenesis and is pharmacologically interceptable with an approved CGRP antagonist, a striking mechanistic cancer-initiation story.
  8. Cellular proximity and conditional coordination in the colorectal and pancreatic tumor microenvironment: a patient-level analysis of multiplexed imaging — Bhadury, S. et al.
    Carefully separates proximity, local composition, and conditional coordination in multiplexed tumor imaging data, showing these distinct spatial statistics can disagree and give different biological conclusions in colorectal and pancreatic cancer.
  9. Beyond the gene: contextualizing novel isoforms through pathway analysis in long-read single-cell RNA sequencing — Doyle, P. H. et al.
    CIPI contextualizes novel isoforms discovered via long-read single-cell RNA-seq by building expression-based neighborhoods for pathway inference, addressing the gap between isoform discovery and functional interpretation.
  10. Microscale bulk segregant analysis — Bruni, G. N. et al.
    A 96-well liquid-handling adaptation of bulk segregant analysis in yeast dramatically increases throughput for QTL mapping across many crosses and environmental conditions simultaneously.

Quick mentions

  1. A zebrafish ribosomopathy links Ddx49-dependent ribosome biogenesis to differential failure of population expansion among pigment cell lineages — Liang, Y. et al.
    A zebrafish ribosomopathy mutant reveals that baseline differences in rRNA processing between pigment cell lineages explain cell-type-specific vulnerability to ribosome biogenesis defects.
  2. Pulmonary Tuberculosis Is Associated with Body Site-Specific Alterations in the Respiratory and Gut Microbiome in Uganda — Mbabazi, M. et al.
    Body-site-specific microbiome alterations (sputum vs stool) are associated with pulmonary tuberculosis in a Ugandan cohort, though effects are confounded by sequencing platform.
  3. A spatial topology atlas of type I myofibers in porcine skeletal muscle reveals local slow-oxidative niches associated with meat quality traits — Shen, Z. et al.
    A spatial topology atlas of slow-oxidative myofibers in pig muscle shows fiber spatial organization is an independent phenotype layer predicting meat quality traits.
  4. Non-exonic read content reorganises lncRNA co-expression networks in renal and other cancers — Youssef, G. et al.
    An unprocessed-RNA alignment artifact (non-exonic read fraction) turns out to dominate lncRNA co-expression network structure across many TCGA cancer types, a cautionary methodological finding.
  5. NoiTox: A Machine Learning Strategy for Peptide Toxicity Prediction Reveals Label Noise in Benchmark Datasets — Almeida, G. O. et al.
    NoiTox flags substantial label noise in peptide toxicity benchmark datasets while showing physicochemical descriptors remain highly informative predictors.
  6. An integrated data exploration engine of knowledge, expression and genetic association for human transposable elements — Jiang, X. et al.
    TE-Dee integrates literature, expression and GTEx eQTL data into a curated knowledge resource for human transposable elements.
  7. A Benchmark of Unsupervised Circadian Phase Inference Methods for Bulk Transcriptomic Data — Purohit, S. et al.
    Benchmarks ten unsupervised circadian phase inference methods on transcriptomic data, finding CHIRAL and clock-gene baselines most accurate but performance highly dataset-dependent.
  8. Poisoning the corpora of protein design systems during pre-training and retrieval — Charalampos Koilakos et al.
    Demonstrates that protein language model pre-training corpora and retrieval-augmented generation systems are vulnerable to data poisoning attacks that reliably induce trigger-dependent sequence generation.
  9. Constructed Negatives Shape the Evaluation of Sequence-Based Protein–Protein Interaction Models — Durand, E. et al.
    Shows that protein-protein interaction model rankings are highly sensitive to how negative training/test examples are constructed, a methodological warning for the PPI prediction field.
  10. Pre-binning correction of chimeric contigs reduces reference-discordant gene annotations in near-complete metagenome-assembled genomes — Ding, Y. et al.
    DeepMM detects chimeric contig misassemblies in metagenome-assembled genomes before binning, reducing reference-discordant gene and virulence-factor annotations in near-complete MAGs.

title: Thu Oct 15: Virtual knockouts expose aging's regulatory noise, engineered chromatin states crack AMD genetics, and sequence-only super-enhancer grammar
summary: 173 new papers. Deep dives: Deep learning-based virtual perturbation reveals increasing heterogeneity of gene regulatory responses with aging; Engineered regulatory states resolve context-dependent genetics in macular degeneration; Decoding super-enhancer regulatory grammar and pathogenic gain-of-function variants directly from DNA sequence; Surrogate variables and the risk of overfitting in neuropsychiatric gene expression analyses; Predicting Unseen Scientific Interactions: Conditional Flow Models Hallucinate Non-Additive Effects
notes_html:
Deep dives

  1. Deep learning-based virtual perturbation reveals increasing heterogeneity of gene regulatory responses with aging — Yongjian He et al.
    A deep-learning virtual-perturbation framework reveals that gene regulatory responses become progressively more heterogeneous with age across four species, linking stochastic damage accumulation to loss of regulatory robustness — a striking systems-level view of aging built entirely on unperturbed single-cell transcriptomes.
  2. Engineered regulatory states resolve context-dependent genetics in macular degeneration — Metzner, E. et al.
    Using CRISPRa multiome Perturb-seq to engineer regulatory states in RPE-1 cells, this paper shows how TF-driven chromatin priming can expose hidden AMD GWAS variant effects, offering a general design principle for making disease-relevant regulatory programs experimentally accessible.
  3. Decoding super-enhancer regulatory grammar and pathogenic gain-of-function variants directly from DNA sequence — Liang, Y. et al.
    Borzoi-SE reformulates super-enhancer discovery as sequence-based object detection, decoding regulatory grammar and pinpointing a single non-coding variant that creates a de novo GR motif driving a cardiac super-enhancer — elegant mechanistic dissection of enhancer logic from DNA alone.
  4. Surrogate variables and the risk of overfitting in neuropsychiatric gene expression analyses — Hoang, D. et al.
    A rigorous audit shows that surrogate variable analysis, a near-ubiquitous covariate-adjustment tool in transcriptomics, can inflate false positives and actually reduce cross-cohort reproducibility — a methodologically important cautionary result for anyone doing differential expression analysis.
  5. Predicting Unseen Scientific Interactions: Conditional Flow Models Hallucinate Non-Additive Effects — Sam Gijsen et al.
    A careful dissection of when conditional flow-matching models genuinely recover versus hallucinate gene-gene and drug interaction effects in extrapolation settings, directly relevant to the reliability of perturbation-prediction models used across single-cell and combinatorial screening.

Briefs

  1. Chromosome 7 gain establishes a just-right WNT signaling state during colorectal tumorigenesis — Zaalberg, I. C. et al.
    Chromosome 7 gain emerges as an adaptive 'just-right' dosage mechanism that tempers excessive WNT activity after APC loss, reframing aneuploidy as fine-tuning rather than brute-force amplification during colorectal tumor evolution.
  2. Bayesian phylogenetics with incomplete lineage tracing data — Zwaans, A. et al.
    A mechanistic model of CRISPR barcode dropout integrated into Bayesian phylogenetics (BEAST2) lets sparse lineage-tracing data be used without filtering, recovering higher and more accurate growth-rate estimates in cell lineage experiments.
  3. Dissection of Polycomb complexes reveals canonical PRC1-independent 3D chromatin interactions — Huseyin, M. K. et al.
    Systematic Polycomb subunit degron experiments overturn the assumption that canonical PRC1 is required for Polycomb-mediated 3D chromatin interactions, revealing a more redundant architecture underlying chromatin organization.
  4. Activation of Disease-Associated Polycystin-1 Mutants by Binding of Stalk-derived Agonist Peptides — Joshi, K. et al.
    A careful eQTL analysis shows that common cis-regulatory variation does not explain why some chromosome 21 genes deviate from the expected 1.5x dosage in trisomy 21, narrowing the search for real buffering mechanisms in Down syndrome.
  5. STARgrid: an open-source pipeline from Visium HD sequencing reads to count matrices — Hung, L.-H. et al.
    STARgrid provides the first open-source, faster alternative to Space Ranger for Visium HD processing, with molecule-level resolution improvements that measurably track cancer gene expression better than the proprietary tool.
  6. Systemic control and inter-organ communication of ovarian aging — Iqbal, S. et al.
    Heterochronic ovary transplantation and parabiosis experiments show ovarian aging is bidirectionally plastic and systemically regulated, identifying the ovary as an active node in an inter-organ aging network with therapeutic implications for fertility.
  7. Trp53 heterozygosity defines novel states impacting tumor plasticity and progression in Kras-initiated non-small cell lung cancer — V, M. et al.
    Single-cell transcriptomics across Trp53 dosage states in Kras-driven lung cancer shows that Trp53 heterozygosity—not just full loss—expands tumor cell-state plasticity, with human-validated prognostic signatures relevant to precision oncology.
  8. The Human Gut Cell Atlas v1.0: A Unified, Community-BuiltReference of Cellular Diversity Across the Gut — Kimler, K. et al.
    A community-built Human Gut Cell Atlas of ~1M cells with standardized taxonomy and metadata management establishes a much-needed reference for reproducible intestinal single-cell analysis across health and disease.
  9. Representing biological concepts as directions in foundation model embeddings — Shamail, A. et al.
    Concept Activation Vectors turn biological foundation model embeddings into interpretable, reusable directions—recovering GO/EC annotations in protein models and cancer-associated expression axes in single-cell embeddings without new predictors.
  10. Optimizing copy number profiles for tumor cell phylogeny inference from low-coverage single-cell sequencing data — Ahmed, N. et al.
    A systematic study shows that bin size choice for inferring copy-number profiles from low-coverage single-cell DNA-seq dramatically affects tumor phylogeny accuracy, with a proposed computational method to select optimal bins.

Quick mentions

  1. A single epigenetic repressor controls opposing developmental tempos in human neural and cranial neural crest lineages — Bell, O. et al.
    ZNF462 is shown to act as a single epigenetic repressor that simultaneously decelerates neural progenitor differentiation and accelerates neural crest specification, redefining Weiss-Kruszka syndrome as a developmental-tempo disorder.
  2. Revealing pan-cancer clonal niches of T cells from single-cell RNA sequencing using contrastive learning — Shorer, O. et al.
    CloneTrast uses contrastive learning to infer T-cell clonal organization from scRNA-seq alone, identifying an NK-like clonal niche linked to poor immunotherapy response across 16 cancer types.
  3. Probabilistic AI models outperform numerical weather prediction models on record breaking heat extremes — Jakob Benjamin Wessel et al.
    Probabilistic AI weather models are shown to outperform physics-based NWP ensembles even on record-breaking heat extremes once evaluation is done properly—an important lesson in benchmarking methodology outside biology.
  4. Sexual reproduction impacts vertebrate organ aging — Chen, J. et al.
    Lifelong mating in killifish reshapes liver, brain and gut aging transcriptomes in a sex-specific way, with echoes in human plasma proteomic aging clocks—an underexplored link between reproduction and organismal aging.
  5. Dog-human gene network colocalization links synaptic signalling and ubiquitination to compulsive disorders — Tengvall, K. et al.
    Combining dog and human GWAS for compulsive disorder reveals a 165-gene network undetectable in humans alone, showcasing companion animals as a powerful amplifier for complex trait gene discovery.
  6. An epigenetic palimpsest: the King penguin's blood methylome reveals conserved hematopoietic ageing — Hukkanen, M. et al.
    King penguin blood methylomes reveal a conserved hematopoietic stem-cell aging signature that transfers to humans and is robust to blood cell composition, suggesting an evolutionarily ancient layer of vertebrate aging.
  7. Convergent genome evolution reveals shared routes to salt tolerance in flowering plants — Wimalagunasekara, S. et al.
    Comparative genomics across 232 angiosperm genomes finds convergent molecular routes to halophytism, including recurrent positive selection at identical amino acid sites across independent lineages.
  8. Towards standards for analysing structural variants from short-read whole genome sequencing data — Slimmer, J. C. et al.
    A rigorous benchmarking study finds that popular ensemble SV-calling pipelines (e.g., GATK-SV) are substantially less accurate than their best constituent tools, with implications for major population SV databases.
  9. Imputing relative abundances via Gaussian random fields — Shternshis, A. et al.
    A Gaussian random field model for imputing compositional microbiome data handles zero-inflation and temporal/multivariate structure, improving longitudinal gut microbiome reconstruction and downstream disease prediction.
  10. Cross-species analysis identifies APOBEC3-associated spliceosomal snRNA hypermutability — Xue, J. et al.
    Cross-species analysis links APOBEC3 activity, rather than R-loop formation alone, to the unusually high mutation rates of spliceosomal snRNA genes in primates.

title: Mon Oct 12: Bidirectional state-space genome models, the MAPK pathway under massive mutational scrutiny, and chromatin-opening transcription factors
summary: 156 new papers. Deep dives: Cerberus: bidirectional state space blocks improve accuracy and efficiency of regulatory sequence models; Massively scaled variant effect mapping across the MAPK pathway reveals the importance of molecular and cellular context; High-throughput identification of chromatin-opening transcription factors; Inferring ecDNA Evolution from Allele Frequency Spectra; Concurrent de novo inference of cell types and gene regulatory networks with NetMap
notes_html:
Deep dives

  1. Cerberus: bidirectional state space blocks improve accuracy and efficiency of regulatory sequence models — Kelley, D. R. et al.
    Cerberus replaces transformer blocks with bidirectional state-space layers in a Borzoi-style sequence-to-function model, beating Borzoi and trading leads with AlphaGenome on eQTL/sQTL/paQTL benchmarks while being far more compute-efficient.
  2. Massively scaled variant effect mapping across the MAPK pathway reveals the importance of molecular and cellular context — Simon, J. J. et al.
    503,099 variant-effect measurements across 17 RAS-MAPK pathway proteins reveal thousands of novel dominant-negative variants and show HSP90 buffers two-thirds of missense effects, illuminating how cellular context shapes signaling networks.
  3. High-throughput identification of chromatin-opening transcription factors — Keith, A. et al.
    A CRISPRa screen of 60 developmental TFs with joint RNA/ATAC profiling in 140,000 single cells dissects which TFs can open chromatin de novo versus requiring cooperating co-TFs, addressing how regulatory programs establish enhancers during fate transitions.
  4. Inferring ecDNA Evolution from Allele Frequency Spectra — Dameracharla, B. et al.
    ecEvol infers ecDNA emergence timing, selection strength and clonal dominance from bulk WGS allele-frequency spectra, showing oncogene-bearing ecDNAs emerge earlier and predict worse survival.
  5. Concurrent de novo inference of cell types and gene regulatory networks with NetMap — Hartebrodt, A. et al.
    NetMap jointly infers single-cell-resolution GRNs and clusters cells by shared regulatory programs rather than relying on pre-assigned cell types, tackling the core challenge of regulatory network inference from scRNA-seq.

Briefs

  1. A unified framework for quantitative splicing and transcript prediction — Jaganathan, K. et al.
    SpliceAI2 reconstructs full transcripts from sequence end-to-end and substantially improves detection and quantification of splice-altering variants, explaining about 15% of excess rare-disease genetic burden.
  2. STEER-seq: a recombinase based platform for pooled multimodal single-cell perturbation screening — Migliori, V. et al.
    STEER-seq uses site-specific recombinase integration to eliminate copy-number confounds in pooled TF overexpression screens, mapping TF-driven chromatin and GRN rewiring at scale in hiPSCs.
  3. Systematic mapping of enhancers, silencers, and topological elements with prime editing deletion screens — Cai, X. S. et al.
    Swap-seq combines pooled prime-editing deletions with flow sorting to systematically classify enhancers, silencers and topological elements, discovering an HDAC-mediated silencer class.
  4. Disrupted chromatin architecture blocks B lymphopoiesis in Down syndrome — Liao, Z. et al.
    A new single-cell multi-omic assay shows 3D chromatin architecture is primed ahead of transcription in human fetal hematopoiesis, with trisomy 21 disrupting an EBF1-centered loop circuit.
  5. scPRIME-seq uncovers synchronized multimodal molecular collapse facilitated by pre-neoplastic epigenetic burden in prostate cancer — Li, S. et al.
    scPRIME-seq profiles transcriptome, genome and methylome jointly in over 400,000 prostate tumor cells, revealing a tipping point coupling aneuploidy onset with genome-wide methylomic change.
  6. Scalable methylome-transcriptome profiling resolves clonal organization in human hematopoiesis — Shao, J. et al.
    Droplet-MT enables scalable joint transcriptome-methylome profiling that reconstructs clonal lineages without genotyping, resolving malignant clone dynamics through AML treatment.
  7. SORT disentangles multilevel gene programs across heterogeneous spatial transcriptomic atlases — Zhang, L. et al.
    SORT disentangles patient-specific, subtype-shared, and region-associated gene expression programs across heterogeneous spatial transcriptomic atlases, linking programs to survival in PDAC.
  8. DeSPA uncovers genes with cross-state spatial pattern remodeling and coordinated spatial programs across multi-slice spatial transcriptomics atlases — Wen, H. et al.
    DeSPA statistically detects genes whose spatial expression pattern remodels across disease or developmental states, revealing coordinated spatial programs in embryogenesis and tissue injury.
  9. Niche-dependent epistasis within the cancer genome shapes metastatic fitness — Liu, X. et al.
    Combinatorial CRISPR screening in vivo shows the tissue niche reshapes which gene-by-gene epistatic interactions promote metastasis, demonstrating organismal-level GxGxE.
  10. Scalable fold-change estimation from microbial metagenomics — Teichman, S. et al.
    fastEmu makes rigorous fold-change and differential abundance testing for microbial metagenomics orders of magnitude faster while preserving error-rate control.

Quick mentions

  1. TorPause: Efficient Static Organ Preservation for Transplants — Bhadury, J. et al.
    A dual PI3K-mTOR inhibitor plus a mitochondria-targeted H2S donor induces reversible metabolic arrest and improves rat liver transplant outcomes after severe ischemia.
  2. Autonomous AI agents discover reverse transcriptases with tandem repeat arrays — Yoon, P. H. et al.
    Autonomous Claude Code agents surveying 1.9 billion protein clusters discovered a novel family of jumbo-phage reverse transcriptases with tandem repeat arrays.
  3. A cellular atlas of Astyanax mexicanus embryogenesis reveals principles of developmental microevolution — Roig Puiggros, S. et al.
    A single-nucleus atlas across two Astyanax mexicanus morphs reveals mosaic heterochronic shifts across tissues during cavefish development.
  4. The dark transcriptome mouse organogenesis cell atlas — Liu, M. et al.
    The first comprehensive single-nucleus atlas of noncoding RNAs across mouse organogenesis reveals coordination between tRNA supply and codon demand.
  5. Fluid transport properties dominate blastocyst expansion over mechanics — Dagher, L. et al.
    Microfluidics, machine learning and biophysical modeling show osmotic fluid-transport dynamics, not mechanical constraints, dominate mouse blastocyst lumen expansion cycles.
  6. GRASS-MIL: graph-based representation and discovery of phenotype-associated spatial structures with multiple instance learning — Rabuzin, L. et al.
    GRASS-MIL exactly decomposes spatial-transcriptomics phenotype predictions into signed contributions from cellular neighborhoods across CosMx, Xenium and MERFISH platforms.
  7. Scalable localization of clustering instability for spatial transcriptomics — Wu, W. et al.
    InSTability quantifies per-spot clustering instability across random seeds in spatial transcriptomics, showing it propagates into inconsistent differential expression results.
  8. DECONVersation: Single Cell Foundation Model-Derived Embeddings for Robust Cell Type Deconvolution of Bulk RNA-seq — Oku, A. et al.
    DECONVersation repurposes single-cell foundation model embeddings for bulk RNA-seq cell-type deconvolution, robust to batch effects without explicit marker genes.
  9. Perturb-Seqr: Signature Search Engine Integrating Connectivity Mapping Resources — Taub, L. D. et al.
    Perturb-Seqr integrates nine Connectivity Mapping resources into one unified search engine of 450,271 gene sets for drug and target discovery.

title: Fri Oct 9: Perturb-seq operators that don't generalize, asynchronous fate restriction in mouse embryos, and temperature-robust morphogen gradients
summary: 115 new papers. Deep dives: Additive-input encoding fails operator-level target-held-out prediction on current Perturb-seq screens; Lineage tracing reveals asynchronous fate restriction in mouse embryos and stem cell-derived embryo models; Predictive Multiplicity in Cell-Fate Assignment: Label-Free Rashomon Sets and the Limits of Per-Cell Certification; Temperature scaling of developmental tempo reveals reaction-dominated morphogen patterning; Protein Language Model-Conditioned Graph Neural Networks for Multitask GPCR Ligand Activity Prediction
notes_html:
Deep dives

  1. Additive-input encoding fails operator-level target-held-out prediction on current Perturb-seq screens — Fullmer, K. et al.
    A rigorous negative result showing that fixed additive-input linear operators fail to generalize to held-out perturbation targets in Perturb-seq screens, directly challenging a common modeling assumption underlying GRN inference from perturbation data.
  2. Lineage tracing reveals asynchronous fate restriction in mouse embryos and stem cell-derived embryo models — Liu, Y. et al.
    Combining DNA Typewriter lineage recording with tetraploid complementation to build high-resolution single-cell genealogies reveals that fate restriction in mouse embryos is progressive and asynchronous, with cell identity alone failing to predict lineage history.
  3. Predictive Multiplicity in Cell-Fate Assignment: Label-Free Rashomon Sets and the Limits of Per-Cell Certification — Arjun Bhupatiraju et al.
    A careful statistical dissection of predictive multiplicity in trajectory inference shows that label-free Rashomon-set certification does not improve per-cell fate-assignment reliability over a model's own confidence, a cautionary methodological result for the single-cell trajectory field.
  4. Temperature scaling of developmental tempo reveals reaction-dominated morphogen patterning — Capek, D. et al.
    Elegant quantitative developmental biology showing that morphogen gradients in medaka embryos remain correctly scaled across temperature-driven changes in developmental tempo because patterning operates in a reaction-dominated regime rather than a diffusion-dominated one.
  5. Protein Language Model-Conditioned Graph Neural Networks for Multitask GPCR Ligand Activity Prediction — De, M. et al.
    AmbiDose introduces per-cell, expression-aware removal budgets for ambient RNA contamination in droplet scRNA-seq, substantially outperforming existing decontamination approaches on cross-species and marker-leakage benchmarks.

Briefs

  1. STAVelo: deciphering spatiotemporal cellular dynamics via spatial RNA velocity inference from spatial transcriptomics data — Li, S. et al.
    STAVelo extends RNA velocity to spatial transcriptomics with a graph-attention model, accurately recovering spatial developmental gradients across brain, kidney, heart and placenta datasets.
  2. HyperCom: a hypergraph-based method to infer cell-resolved cell-cell communication — Moy, J. K. et al.
    HyperCom uses hypergraph diffusion to infer cell-resolved, rather than cell-type-aggregated, ligand-receptor communication, reducing a common source of bias in cell-cell communication analysis.
  3. scStable: assessing scRNA-seq analysis stability under bulk-derived between-sample variation — Jiang, C. et al.
    scStable injects bulk-derived between-sample variation into single-sample scRNA-seq references to assess discovery stability, addressing the common but under-tested problem of single-sample scRNA-seq generalizability.
  4. PHC2-Dependent PRC1 Assemblies Stabilize Motor Neuron Hox Codes — Miller, A. K. et al.
    Shows that PHC2-dependent PRC1 subnuclear condensates are required to stabilize Hox transcriptional boundaries and motor neuron segmental identity, linking chromatin 3D assembly to gene regulatory output.
  5. Heterochromatin protein 1α acts as an essential stabilizer of chromatin packing domains — Kuo, T. et al.
    Demonstrates that HP1 alpha crosslinking is essential for maintaining heterochromatic cores of chromatin packing domains and for enabling stress-responsive transcriptional reprogramming.
  6. Unlocking the Regulatory Genome by ARGUS: An Evidence-Constrained Agentic Framework for Interpreting Single Nucleotide Variants — Pratik Dutta et al.
    ARGUS pairs 458 DNABERT TF-binding models with an LLM-mediated evidence-gathering agent to interpret noncoding GWAS variants, showing how uncertainty-aware tool orchestration can resolve conflicting regulatory evidence without hallucination.
  7. A gene-centric analysis of copy number variation reveals tumour suppressor modulation of cancer risk and novel associations with common diseases — Matthews, S. et al.
    A gene-centric, rather than region-based, CNV analysis identifies novel whole-gene deletions, including a germline extension of the 13q14 somatic association, linked to cancer risk and other common diseases.
  8. Robust ORF Deconvolution from Multiple Ribo-seq Datasets with Group LASSO Penalty — Maidhof, K. et al.
    PRICE 2 applies group-LASSO deconvolution across multiple Ribo-seq datasets to resolve weakly translated and overlapping ORFs, substantially boosting discovery of cryptic MHC-I peptide sources.
  9. Dynamic Schlafen 11 (SLFN11) expression revealed by single-cell RNA sequencing of clonal human cancer cells — Taniyama, D. et al.
    Single-cell profiling reveals dynamic, heterogeneous SLFN11 expression linked to a stress-response state, exposing a hidden determinant of chemotherapy resistance invisible to bulk assays.
  10. Limitations of Genomic Foundation Models for Decoding Regulatory Mechanisms in ALS — Talukder, A. et al.
    A sobering benchmark showing that AlphaGenome fails to recover measured splicing QTL effect sizes and effector genes in ALS, highlighting current limits of genomic foundation models for regulatory variant interpretation.

Quick mentions

  1. Sketching the SRA: experiment-wide similarity search across 4.8 million metagenomes — Faure, R. et al.
    Releases experiment-wide sketches and an all-pairs similarity matrix for 4.8 million SRA metagenomes, enabling unprecedented scale metagenome comparison and metadata correction.
  2. Inhibitory Nectin-2/TIGIT interactions between CD163+ macrophages and CD8+ T cells in spatially defined immune niches associate with poor outcomes in neuroblastoma — Borst, A. L. et al.
    Spatial imaging mass cytometry identifies CD163+ macrophage-CD8+ T cell Nectin-2/TIGIT interactions in immune niches that correlate with poor neuroblastoma outcomes.
  3. Beyond Action Entropy: Quotient-Space Exploration for Genome-Scale Metabolic Model Repair — Xuan Gong et al.
    QuotientPO reframes genome-scale metabolic model repair as quotient-space exploration over mechanistically equivalent edits, improving mechanism-level discovery under verifier-induced equivalence.
  4. CCT2 expression marks a translation-activated state in sporadic ALS motor neurons and is associated with functional decline — Bhandary, P. et al.
    CCT2 is identified as a single-gene marker of a translation-activated molecular state in sporadic ALS motor neurons, offering a candidate biological stratifier for a genetically heterogeneous disease.
  5. Sex-dependent DNA methylation in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis — Kim, Y. J. et al.
    A large epigenome-wide meta-analysis finds sex-dependent ALS methylation signals at immune, metabolic and ion-channel loci invisible to sex-stratified analyses alone.
  6. REFinder: Mining new enzymes from metagenomes — Prabakaran, R. et al.
    REFinder uses a DNA language model to triage metagenomic reads before assembly, recovering thousands of novel, homology-invisible enzymes far more cheaply than full-community assembly.
  7. A ribosomal pseudouridine drives an oncogenic translation program — Faucher-Giguere, L. et al.
    A single snoRNA-guided rRNA pseudouridine modification is shown to selectively reprogram translation of cancer-related mRNAs in ovarian cancer cells via a 'sno-balling' amplification cascade.
  8. Loss of the Y chromosome drives basal identity and metastatic potential via epigenetic reprogramming in pancreatic cancer — Dorsch, M. et al.
    Loss of the Y chromosome is identified as a recurrent driver of EMT and metastatic basal identity in pancreatic cancer through epigenetic reprogramming, affecting about half of male PDAC patients.
  9. Placental cis-eQTL analysis identifies preeclampsia-dependent genetic regulation at promoters — Yazgeldi Gunaydin, G. et al.
    Promoter-level, but not gene-level, cis-eQTL analysis in placenta reveals preeclampsia-dependent genotype interactions missed by standard gene-level eQTL mapping.
  10. An androgen-derived transcriptional state reveals signaling and mitochondrial vulnerabilities in cancer — Miao, Y. et al.
    An androgen-derived transcriptional signature, projected across cancer cell lines, reveals unexpected EGFR-resistance and mitochondrial dependency relationships independent of cancer lineage.

title: Wed Oct 7: Sparse model discovery for gene oscillators, identifiable optimal transport for cell transitions, and why spatial RNA and protein disagree on checkpoint markers
summary: 92 new papers. Deep dives: RI-SINDy: Regulation-Informed Sparse Model Discovery in Biological Gene Networks; Identifiable inverse optimal transport for single-cell state transitions; RNA and protein are not interchangeable in single-cell spatial multi-omics; MERFISH-based pooled genetic screening reveals cell non-autonomous phenotypes in intact tissue; Circular Data Analysis for Spatial Omics
notes_html:
Deep dives

  1. RI-SINDy: Regulation-Informed Sparse Model Discovery in Biological Gene Networks — Lucenti, N. J. et al.
    Introduces RI-SINDy, a sparse model-discovery method that removes collinear Hill-type regulatory terms before regression, substantially improving recovery of gene regulatory network dynamics from oscillatory time-series data like Hes1 and NF-kB.
  2. Identifiable inverse optimal transport for single-cell state transitions — Dong, H. et al.
    Proposes a semi-relaxed inverse optimal transport framework (UOT-IOT) that restores identifiability of target-state programme effects in single-cell state transitions, with strong gains over balanced OT on real perturbation and lineage data.
  3. RNA and protein are not interchangeable in single-cell spatial multi-omics — Cervilla, S. et al.
    A rigorous paired Xenium RNA/protein comparison across ~1.8M cells showing spatial organization is far more discordant between modalities than abundance, a cautionary result for anyone treating spatial transcriptomics as a protein proxy.
  4. MERFISH-based pooled genetic screening reveals cell non-autonomous phenotypes in intact tissue — Jin, K. et al.
    An amplification-free MERFISH pooled screening method that jointly reads perturbation identity, transcriptome, and spatial neighborhood in intact tissue, revealing cell-non-autonomous effects of hepatocyte perturbations on immune and vascular niches.
  5. Circular Data Analysis for Spatial Omics — Shin, J. et al.
    A practical methods guide for handling circular/periodic quantities (circadian phase, cell-cycle position) in single-cell and spatial omics, with worked examples showing when standard linear or spatial models mislead.

Briefs

  1. Identifiability of a linear dynamical reaction-diffusion system with directed interactions from the second-order statistics of a single snapshot — Pirmin Schlicke
    Shows that directed cell-cell interaction structure in reaction-diffusion models (e.g., tumor-immune tissue) is recoverable from the wavenumber-dependence of a single spatial snapshot's second-order statistics, not from means or simple covariance.
  2. Conservation of gene co-expression networks and neuropsychiatric-neurological disease gene programs between mouse and human frontal cortex at single-cell resolution — Sun, Q.-Q. et al.
    Large-scale single-cell comparison of gene co-expression networks between mouse and human prefrontal cortex finds only modest single-gene partner conservation but strong module-level preservation, with implications for translating GRN findings across species.
  3. Genetic dissection of DNA damage response pathways reveals divergent modulation of PD-1 blockade response in colorectal cancer — Fece de la Cruz, F. et al.
    A systematic in vivo DDR gene screen shows pathway-specific (not uniform) effects on anti-PD-1 response in MSS colorectal cancer, identifying ATM inhibition as a rational immunotherapy-sensitizing combination.
  4. Linkage disequilibrium moderates how evolving genetic background shapes variant-level architecture — Lee, H. et al.
    A population-genetic model coupling variant evolution to linkage-disequilibrium background shows that frequency-dependent effect-size patterns can arise from demographic history alone, without invoking differential selection strength across populations.
  5. Intraindividual longitudinal changes of the proteome reveal dynamic markers of biological aging — Lermer, R. et al.
    A longitudinal (not just cross-sectional) plasma proteomic aging clock in >4,000 individuals links within-person risk-factor changes to age-acceleration transitions and mortality, with Mendelian randomization support for causal aging proteins.
  6. Integrative genetic and transcriptomic analysis identifies candidate genes and compounds for Fragile X syndrome and autism spectrum disorder — Zhang, W. et al.
    Integrates population genetics, twin discordance, and FMRP-QTL data to link Fragile X syndrome biology to idiopathic autism's polygenic architecture and prioritize repurposable compounds.
  7. Establishment and characterization of LNCaP-TR-BoM, a bone metastasis-derived prostate cancer cell line with an intermediate AR-attenuated phenotype — Chao, A. et al.
    scRNA-seq and RNAi screening in regenerating planarian eyes identifies DDR collagen receptors and TMEM132 adhesion factors as controllers of progenitor migration and self-organized organ assembly, a nice model for cell fate/differentiation trajectories.
  8. Spatially restricted bmp16 in an extra-embryonic syncytium promotes dorsoventral patterning — Couturier, H. et al.
    Single-nucleus and spatial transcriptomics of the zebrafish yolk syncytial layer uncovers a spatially restricted bmp16 program that patterns the dorsoventral axis from an extra-embryonic compartment, illuminating multinucleate signaling organization.
  9. ASTRA enables zero-shot super-resolution of spatial transcriptomics across capture geometries — Ye, J. et al.
    ASTRA is a cross-platform, zero-shot pretrained model for spatial transcriptomics super-resolution that generalizes across capture geometries (Visium HD, pseudo-Visium) without per-section retraining.
  10. Genomic SEM reveals shared genetic architecture and expands locus discovery for locomotor activity in heterogeneous stock rats — Chitre, A. S. et al.
    Compares Genomic SEM against standard meta-analysis for locus discovery of a heritable behavioral trait across heterogeneous rat cohorts, nearly quadrupling loci found versus pooled GWAS—a methods lesson applicable to multi-cohort omics integration.

Quick mentions

  1. A near-ubiquitous plasmid characterises Second Pandemic Yersinia pestis — Seersholm, F. V. et al.
    Pangenomic analysis of ancient Yersinia pestis genomes finds a near-ubiquitous cryptic plasmid unique to the Black Death-era Second Pandemic, potentially explaining its outsized mortality via expanded vector range.
  2. Genomic classification and immune profiling define mucosal melanoma — Shi, Y. et al.
    Multimodal profiling of 339 mucosal melanoma patients defines four genomic subtypes and implicates CD163+ macrophage-TIM3 signaling as an immunotherapy resistance mechanism.
  3. EPHA4 Regulates the Transition between Mesenchymal and Hybrid States in TNBC — Liu, W. et al.
    EPHA4 loss shifts triple-negative breast cancer cells from mesenchymal to hybrid E/M states, trading invasiveness for enhanced metastatic colonization capacity.
  4. Binding kinetics enable tumor-selective MAPK and growth suppression by a Type 1 RAF Inhibitor — Desaunay, M. et al.
    A Type 1 RAF inhibitor exploits fast on/off binding kinetics to achieve tumor-selective MAPK suppression in RAS/RAF-dimer-driven cancers while sparing normal tissue.
  5. SLC25A28 is a synthetic lethal vulnerability in nucleotide excision repair-deficient cancers — Yang, N. et al.
